pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Add support for getting controller values in public API
pr_body:
Adds a new API to get LE controller info. 
Adds a test and a use of the new API

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/81872

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: ISO: Expose controller buffer size to public API
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
During `bt_enable()` the host reads the controller ISO buffer sizes, but these are not available to the user (the application), as it is only stored in the `bt_dev`. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Expose an API function that returns the size and count of the ISO buffers, as that is valuable information to the application in terms of how much data it wants to send and how often. 

For example if the SDU needs to be fragmented, the application may want to send ISO data at a lower interval, or modify the data, e.g. a lower resolution in sensor data or use a different audio codec. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It is possible to include `hci_core.h` in the application today to do this, but that is not a public header file and is as such not a very good alternative. 

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments: I assume we want to extend this struct whenever the spec defines a new feature set. Eventually this struct can become very large. Is this something we want to do?

It's a good question. Similar to the other `info` structs, it's only stack allocated so it wouldn't be taking up much memory, but might run into stack overflows in some cases I guess. 

An alternative would be to do similar to what I did for ISO where the internal state uses the public state to store information: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn_internal.h#L182-L183

Today we are still doing an allocation + copy, but we could in theory return a `const` pointer directly to that struct, which would effectively require no additional memory.
Do we want to add Filter accept list size to this struct?
I think that would make sense, but the Zephyr host isn't reading that at the moment, so that would be a new feature
